 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIRZAR S. DESAI
Date : 10/07/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of this petition preferred under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the applicant - accused No.2 has prayed to quash and set aside FIR being C.R. I No.11216008220350 of 2022 dated 26.7.2022 lodged before Gandhinagar Sector 7 Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 as well as charge-sheet filed in connection with the impugned FIR for the said offences and Criminal Case No.779 of 2024 filed before Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gandhinagar instituted pursuant to the impugned FIR and charge-sheet with all subsequent proceedings qua the applicant.
2.
At the outset, it is required to be stated that this petition is filed after filing of charge-sheet.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11715/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined 3.

The facts leading to filing of the present petition are stated as under :-
3.1.

One Balwantsinh Vitthalrai Gaekwad, respondent No.2 herein - original informant has filed the impugned FIR wherein he has stated that there was a land admeasuring around 50 Bighas bearing Sim Survey No.601/7 New Survey No.263 situated at village Vadvasa, Tal. Dehgam, Dist. Gandhinagar was owned by him.
The said land was sold in the year 2014 to the present applicant.

However, as consideration for the aforesaid land was not paid to him, he preferred an application for inquiring into the matter and pursuant to the aforesaid inquiry, an undertaking was given by him as well as the books of Notary A. B. Thakore was sent to FSL,
Gandhinagar and upon receipt of the report from FSL, Gandhinagar, the aforesaid undertaking was found to have been forged and it does not bear the signature of the complainant and, therefore, he filed the FIR.

3.2 Though details narrated in the FIR are not elaborately stated, the sum and substance of the FIR is that the aforesaid land independently owned by the complainant was decided to be sold at a rate of Rs.2 Lac per Bigha and, therefore,
total amount of Rs.6 Crore for a parcel of land admeasuring 50 Bighas were to be paid to the complainant by the present applicant.

It was also decided that sum of Rs.1 Crore will be paid as per the Jantri rate and rest of the amount were to be paid through various cheques and as and when the cash amount would be paid, the cheques would be returned to the complainant.
Accordingly, the Sale Deed was executed by paying a sum of Rs.1 Crores by way of different cheques.
Out of Rs.1 Crore, a sum of Rs.35 Lacs were received by NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11715/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined the complainant.
However, remaining amount of Rs.65 Lacs were never paid to the complainant.

Further, cash amount of Rs.75,51,000/- were paid by cash and remaining amount of consideration being Rs.4,05,27,000/- were paid by way of 7 cheques with a condition that as and when the amount is paid in cash, the cheque would be returned.

However,
the aforesaid amount was never paid to the complainant.

Therefore, through one Gopal Shah, the complainant met one Mr. Saharbhai Ramabhai Rabari, a land broker and gave him a Power of Attorney and the said Saharbhai negotiated with the applicant and stated to the complainant that the applicant is ready and willing to repay the amount and, therefore, by believing his version, Civil Suit preferred by the complainant was withdrawn.

Thereafter, as the present applicant did not pay the remaining amount, the said Saharbhai told the complainant that they will have to carry the matter to the High Court and by stating that he took away the original cheques of the amount of Rs.4,05,27,000/- and file containing original documents and filed an application before this Court but ultimately, without knowledge and permission of the complainant, the same was withdrawn from this Court.

Ultimately,
the complainant came to know that the said Saharbhai sided with the present applicant and gave all the original papers and cheques to the applicant.

In the Jagdish Motilal Sheth vs State Of Gujarat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56356123/
2 interregnum period, the applicant got the name of his wife Divyaben, daughter Pujaben and Son Aakash mutated into the land in question.

sentences.text:
Thereafter, on 15.6.2016,
an undertaking was prepared in the name of the complainant stating that for the land in question, there is no outstanding and, therefore, all the litigation would be withdrawn and, therefore, on the basis of the aforesaid Notarized undertaking, by using the same as original, the applicant got a Title Clearance Certificate from a reputed Legal Firm and got NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11715/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined the land converted into Non-Agriculture Land.

Therefore, as the land was got converted into Non-Agriculture after obtaining Title Clearance Certificate, on the basis of forged documents i.e. in the nature of an undertaking, the FIR was registered.
3.3 The said FIR is subject matter of challenge before this Court by way of this petition.

4. Mr. Jal Soli Unwalla, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Maulik Sheth for the applicant submitted that though this petition is filed after filing of charge-sheet, filing of charge-sheet is no bar in considering the application for quashing and in support of this submission, he relied upon various decisions.

However, by now it is well settled that merely because the charge-sheet is filed, same cannot act as bar in considering an application for quashing under Section 528 of the BNSS or Section 482 of the Cr.P.C, as the case may be, the above submission as well as decisions relied upon by learned Senior Counsel Mr. Unwalla are not elaborately mentioned in this order.

4.1 Mr. Unwalla tried to put forward the case by stating that essentially, dispute is of civil nature and to demonstrate that the dispute is of civil nature, he has taken this Court to the entire history of litigation between the parties to indicate that dispute started right from the year 2014.

However, at that time, the suit preferred by the complainant being Special Civil Suit No.172 of 2013 was withdrawn unconditionally by the complainant on 7.8.2013 in view of settlement arrived at between the parties.

It was also pointed out by learned Senior Counsel Mr. Unwalla that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11715/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined the first informant earlier had filed one complaint before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehgam being Criminal Inquiry No.4 of 2013 for the offences punishable under Sections 392, 394, 323, 294(b), 506(2), 120(b) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
However, the learned Magistrate stayed the inquiry under Section 210 of the Cr.P.C. and called for Police report.

Ultimately, even as per the Police Report, the dispute between the parties was settled and, therefore, statement of first informant was also recorded and Criminal Inquiry No.4 of 2013 did not proceed further.

4.2 Learned Senior Counsel Mr. Unwalla has narrated the history of various litigation, disputes,
criminal complaints and their outcome before the Court and then took this Court to the fact that complainant preferred Civil Suit No.138 of 2015 for cancellation of Registered Sale Deed and permanent injunction before the Senior Civil Judge, Gandhinagar for the land in question and the learned Civil Judge rejected interim injunction application Exh.5 which was carried before this Jagdish Motilal Sheth vs State Of Gujarat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56356123/
3

entities.text: Jagdish Motilal Sheth vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Court by way of Appeal From Order No.25 of 2016.
However, even in Appeal From Order No.25 of 2016 also, in view of settlement arrived at between the parties, the same was withdrawn.

4.3 Learned Senior Counsel Mr. Unwalla also pointed out that on 28.8.2015, after the aforesaid settlement, the complainant even preferred one more frivolous complaint before Dehgam Police Station under the provisions of Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code and the said complaint was also closed.

He also narrated the chequered history of the various transactions related to land and tried to submit that the applicant is falsely implicated by the complainant by way of impugned FIR as the dispute between NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11715/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined the parties is of civil in nature and time and again, various settlements have taken place and though the settlement in question was of the year 2016 and was well within the knowledge of the complainant, he did not file any FIR on the basis of the same and all of a sudden, once the land prices are surged and now skyrocketing, with ill-intention, the impugned FIR is filed to extort more money from the applicant.

Therefore, this is a fit case for this Court to prevent abuse and misuse of process of law and, therefore, this Court may entertain this petition and interfere in the further proceedings arising out of the FIR and charge-sheet.
5. I have heard learned advocate appearing for the applicant and perused the record.
On perusal of the record, I found that there are numerous litigation in the past in respect of the land in question.
It is true that on more than one occasion, settlement is arrived at between the parties.
However, the litigation never ended and on perusal of the documents, I found that both the sides have different versions.
Therefore, there is a word against word.

Therefore, at this juncture, when the FIR is registered as back as in the year 2022 for which even the charge- sheet is also filed on 18.2.2024 and when registration of offence and charge-sheet papers would prima facie constitute an offence and it indicates that prima facie offence is made out, it would not be proper on the part of this Court to interfere with the ongoing trial as the veracity of claim and counter claim by the applicant and complainant is a matter of evidence and this Court in a petition under Section 528 of the BNSS is required to examine only to the extent that whether a prima facie offence is made out on bare perusal of the FIR and charge-sheet or not.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11715/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined 6.

Accordingly, upon perusal of FIR as well as charge- sheet papers, the Court funds that there is word against word and it relates to the Title Clearance Certificate obtained on the basis of fraudulent assurance deed and thereafter, the land in question is converted into N.A. and, therefore, without entering or examining the merit any further, as bare reading of the FIR and perusal of charge-sheet papers constitutes prima facie offence, I do not deem it proper to entertain this petition by interfering with the process of on-going trial.
Therefore, the present petition is required to be dismissed and the same is dismissed.

(NIRZAR S. DESAI,J) SAVARIYA Jagdish Motilal Sheth vs State Of Gujarat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56356123/
